newSource.sourceType: public school curriculum plan; the document identifies Kanghsuan book 1
observed: Week 18 / 3-2 includes translating a contextual quantity relation into a linear equation and understanding what a solution means; the listed methods include substitution or enumeration.
The following week / 3-3 lists equality axioms, transposition, and verification.
The plan lists oral questioning, peer discussion, presentation, homework and written assessment.
newSource.limit: This is a school-authored curriculum plan, not Kanghsuan textbook prose, examples, or publisher-authenticated pedagogy. It corroborates one implementation only.

fusionDecisionChangedOrStrengthened: A-7-2 explicitly treats substitution/enumeration as a way to understand or verify candidate solutions, not as a generally efficient method for discovering an unknown solution.
The lesson retains a worked reject/accept pair by substituting candidates into the unchanged original equation and comparing both sides.
Equality-preserving transformations and systematic solving remain in A-7-3; no balance-scale interaction is claimed for A-7-2.
This specific public-school evidence strengthens the source-to-scope rationale. It does not close the Kanghsuan publisher-text evidence slot or authorize upgrading reviewStatus.
